summary: H.R. 9329, titled the 'SEC Reform and Restructuring Act', makes several organizational, procedural, and regulatory changes to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and related bodies. Key areas include enhanced cost-benefit analysis requirements for SEC regulations, increased congressional oversight and testimony, a Government Accountability Office (GAO) audit of SEC cybersecurity and IT, the transfer of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board into an office within the SEC, recurring GAO studies on major rules, minimum public comment periods, clarity on counting multiple violations for enforcement penalties, and internal SEC organizational restructuring.

affected_groups.effect: Must adhere to stricter cost-benefit analysis procedures, conduct post-implementation assessments for major rules, reorganize direct-reporting offices, provide regular congressional testimony, and manage the integration of accounting oversight functions.
Subject to oversight by the new Office of Public Accounting Oversight within the SEC after the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board terminates.
Benefit from longer minimum public comment periods (at least 60 days) on proposed rules and clearer guidelines regarding how multiple regulatory violations and penalties are calculated.

key_provisions: Requires the SEC to conduct thorough cost-benefit analyses, assess cumulative regulatory impacts, utilize its Chief Economist, and establish post-adoption impact assessments and plans for major rules.
Mandates semiannual testimony by the SEC Chairman and annual joint testimony by the Commissioners to specific congressional committees.
Directs the Comptroller General to perform an independent audit of the SEC's IT infrastructure, data handling, and cybersecurity within one year.
Transfers and integrates the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board into the SEC's Office of the Chief Accountant as the Office of Public Accounting Oversight after two years.
Establishes a minimum public comment period of at least 60 days (or 30 days for imminent investor harm) for proposed rulemakings.
Clarifies that separate acts of noncompliance constitute a single violation for penalty purposes if they stem from a common cause, the same misstatement, or a continuing failure to comply.
Requires the SEC Chairman to review the agency's organizational structure and reduce the number of offices and officials reporting directly to the Chairman.

Key areas include enhanced cost-benefit analysis requirements for SEC regulations, increased congressional oversight and testimony, a Government Accountability Office (GAO) audit of SEC cybersecurity and IT, the transfer of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board into an office within the SEC, recurring GAO studies on major rules, minimum public comment periods, clarity on counting multiple violations for enforcement penalties, and internal SEC organizational restructuring.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters the internal operations, regulatory adoption process, enforcement penalty calculations, and structural organization of the SEC and public company accounting oversight.
